question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\sqrt{6}\,x)) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\sqrt{6}\,x)) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{1}{1-{(\sqrt{6}\,x)}^{2}}\cdot {(\sqrt{6}\,x)}^{′} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{1}{1-6{x}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{6} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{1-6{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
